lesson_title: A Drawing Another Team Could Build From
hook_text: If your friend can cut every part from your drawing without asking one question, you have drawn it right.
clip_script: Here is how to make the drawing your team will build from. Choose one face, the front, the one that shows the most: height, width, uprights, braces, the hole for the axle. Choose a scale that fits the page: the frame is 400 by 300, A4 is small, so half size, 1:2. Now draw everything faintly, measuring as you go: outer rectangle, uprights, braces, the hole on the centre line. Stop. Measure it again. Fix it while it is faint. Then press harder and go over every edge you can see. Dashed lines for anything hidden behind. Dash-dot lines crossing through every hole. Now the sizes, in real millimetres, outside the drawing: 300 across, 400 up, 20 for an upright, 50 from the top to the hole. Title block in the corner: name, scale, date. Then the test: hand it to a friend. If they can build it without asking, you are done.
visual_style: Whiteboard A4 outline; a faint frame appears, gets measured, darkens, gains dashed and dash-dot lines, then dimensions and a title block; a hand passes it to another hand.
pacing: Choose, scale, faint, check, darken, special lines, dimensions, title block, test: nine quick beats.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and run the maker's test on your own drawing.
